- On B_{ϱ+ε/2}(x₀) ⊇ B̄_ϱ(x₀) ⊇ spt X we have ζ = 1, so ω−φ = α there. `cycle_const` with r = ϱ+ε/2 gives X(ω−φ) = 0, hence X(ω) = X(φ). This is exactly the supplied steps 6-8: ω−φ = (1−ζ)ω + ζα, and the two pieces are killed by step 6 and step 7 respectively.

subproblems.title: The Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors is a continuous seminorm dominated by the operator norm
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ α α' : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + α') ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm α') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C * ‖α‖) ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note. This child is the already accepted DAG node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1 (Lean declaration Submission.rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props, status accepted, candidate commit f492ba4a003c8f1324077e050d48667ae23c7100). It is proposed here with its byte-identical frozen Lean type, so the runtime reuses it by name and provisions no new worker. In the selected parent it provides step 1 (homogeneity, part (ii)) and step 2 (coefficient norm versus operator norm, part (iii); the constant √(card(Fin n → Fin P)) = P^{n/2} is the parent's constant). Its accepted natural proof follows verbatim.

Source: parent proof, step 1 (Properties of N), with all details filled in.

Notation. e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1. 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, and #𝓙 = Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P). For I ∈ 𝓙, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), in Lean (fun i => e (I i)). F := Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps. By definition
N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. Coefficient vector. For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α); in Lean, v α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => c_I α). The Euclidean norm formula ‖w‖ = √(Σ_I ‖w_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), together with ‖w_I‖² = w_I², gives
   N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α ∈ F.   (∗)

2. Linearity of v. Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form: (α + α')(e_I) = α(e_I) + α'(e_I) and (t·α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I). So, coordinatewise, c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α); both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing. Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α) (WithLp.toLp_add, WithLp.toLp_smul).

3. Proof of (i). By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙:
   N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').

4. Proof of (ii). By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm:
   N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).

5. Coordinate bound. For every I ∈ 𝓙, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
   - If I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖·1 = ‖α‖.
   - Otherwise |c_I(α)| = 0 ≤ ‖α‖.

6. Proof of (iii). Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, c_I(α)² = |c_I(α)|² ≤ ‖α‖² for every I, so Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖². Since √ is monotone and ‖α‖ ≥ 0,
   N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = √(#𝓙)·√(‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.

7. Proof of (iv). Let α, α' ∈ F.
   - By (i), N(α) = N((α − α') + α') ≤ N(α − α') + N(α').
   - α' − α = −(α − α') and N(−β) = N(β) (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg, or (ii) with t = −1). So by (i), N(α') = N((α' − α) + α) ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α).
   Together with (iii), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖. Thus dist(N(α), N(α')) ≤ C·dist(α, α') for all α, α', so N is Lipschitz with the nonnegative constant C (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with K := ⟨C, C ≥ 0⟩), hence continuous.

Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with the constant C of (iii) equal to √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)).

Lean note. A compiled route (about 70 lines, no extra imports):
- Use `classical`, and define c and v with `let`.
- Prove (∗) by `rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq]; unfold covectorEuclideanNorm; congr 1`, then `Finset.sum_congr rfl` with `by_cases hI : StrictMono I` and `simp`.
- Prove linearity by `simp only [v, ← WithLp.toLp_add]` (resp. `← WithLp.toLp_smul`), then `congr 1; funext I; by_cases hI : StrictMono I <;> simp [c, hI]`.
- For step 5, use `α.le_opNorm (fun i => e (I i))` followed by `simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs]`; simp knows that basis vectors have norm 1.
- For step 6, use `Real.sqrt_sq`, `Real.sqrt_mul`, `Real.sqrt_le_sqrt`, `Finset.sum_le_sum` and `pow_le_pow_left₀`.
- For step 7, first rewrite N(α' − α) = N(α − α') by `rw [← neg_sub, covectorEuclideanNorm_neg]`, then apply (i) together with `sub_add_cancel`, `abs_le` and `linarith`. Finish with `(LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul (K := ⟨_, Real.sqrt_nonneg _⟩) hlip).continuous`.
proof_key_steps: Write N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for the coefficient vector v(α) = (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).
v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous, because evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α.
(i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖, which is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and hence continuous, which is (iv).

subproblems.title: Evaluation bound |T(ω)| ≤ r·M_W(T) when tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ r (fact (E1))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) and r ∈ ℝ. Write |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and M_W(T) := T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞]. By Simon 6.2.5, M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal T(φ) over φ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W and |φ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. If M_W(T) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ r for every x ∈ ℝ^P, then |T(ω)| ≤ r·(M_W(T)).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), T.massOn W ≠ ∞ → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * (T.massOn W).toReal

Reuse note. This child is the already accepted DAG node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.eval_mass_bound-a1 (Lean declaration Submission.cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn, status accepted, candidate commit 7a706164baaf42fc7f55751247396a8836928310). It is proposed here with its byte-identical frozen Lean type, so the runtime reuses it by name and provisions no new worker. In the selected parent it is step 3 (mass controls evaluations), applied with U = W = ℝ^P (univ). For U = univ, X.massOn univ is by definition X.mass, and X.mass < ∞ gives X.massOn univ ≠ ∞. Its accepted natural proof follows verbatim.

Source: parent proof, elementary fact (E1).
1. (Homogeneity.) Let t ∈ ℝ and α be an n-covector. Then (t•α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I) for every I : Fin n → Fin P, so Σ_I [StrictMono I]((t•α)(e_I))² = t²·S with S := Σ_I [StrictMono I](α(e_I))² ≥ 0. Hence |t•α| = √(t²S) = |t|·√S = |t|·|α|. Also |α| ≥ 0, being a square root, and |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (r ≥ 0.) By hypothesis 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ r.
3. Put M := T.massOn W and m := M.toReal ≥ 0. Since M ≠ ∞, for every real a, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ M implies a ≤ m (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal).
4. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix ε > 0 and let s := r + ε > 0. Let ω' := s⁻¹ • ω, an element of TestFormOn U n (a submodule) whose underlying form is x ↦ s⁻¹•ω(x). Then tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, since the tsupport of a scalar multiple is contained in the tsupport. By step 1, |ω'(x)| = s⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ r/s ≤ 1 for all x. Hence ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Likewise −ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, since it has the same tsupport and |−ω'(x)| = |ω'(x)|.
5. (Bound.) By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(T ω') ≤ M and ofReal(T(−ω')) ≤ M. By step 3, T ω' ≤ m and −T ω' = T(−ω') ≤ m (T is linear), i.e. |T ω'| ≤ m. By linearity T ω' = s⁻¹·T ω, so |T ω| = s·|T ω'| ≤ (r + ε)·m.
6. (Conclusion.) Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and m ≥ 0, |T ω| ≤ r·m = r·(T.massOn W).toReal.
proof_key_steps: For ε > 0, both ±(r+ε)⁻¹ω are admissible for M_W(T).
le_massOn and M_W(T) ≠ ∞ give |T ω| ≤ (r+ε)·M_W(T).toReal.
Let ε → 0.

subproblems.title: Test forms are Lipschitz in the Euclidean coefficient norm
subproblems.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn U k: a C^∞ k-form on ℝ^P with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ U). For a k-covector β write |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β, the Euclidean coefficient norm of Simon 6.1.15. Then there is a real number c ≥ 0 such that |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c·dist(x, y) for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U k), ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ x y : Euclid P, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y) ≤ c * dist x y
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 4 of the parent proof (the Lipschitz constant c of the fixed test form, measured in the Euclidean coefficient norm), stated for an arbitrary degree k and an arbitrary domain U. The comparison of the coefficient norm with the operator norm (parent step 2) is supplied by part (iii) of the sibling norm_props.

Notation. For a k-covector β (an element of Covector (Euclid P) k, i.e. a continuous alternating k-linear form on ℝ^P), |β| := covectorEuclideanNorm β and ‖β‖ is its operator norm. On ℝ^P, ‖·‖ is the Euclidean norm and dist(x, y) = ‖x − y‖ (dist_eq_norm). Write w := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) : ℝ^P → Covector (Euclid P) k for the underlying form of ω.

1. (Coefficient norm versus operator norm.) By the sibling norm_props, part (iii), applied to (P, k), there is a real C ≥ 0 such that |β| ≤ C·‖β‖ for every k-covector β.

2. (Smoothness.) Membership ω ∈ TestFormOn U k means IsTestForm w ∧ tsupport w ⊆ U, where IsTestForm w = IsSmoothForm w ∧ HasCompactSupport w and IsSmoothForm w = ContDiff ℝ ∞ w. Since the smoothness order ∞ is nonzero, w is differentiable at every point of ℝ^P (ContDiff.differentiable). Its Fréchet derivative Dw := fderiv ℝ w : ℝ^P → (ℝ^P →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) k) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv).

3. (The derivative is bounded.) Dw has compact support because w does (HasCompactSupport.fderiv: the support of Dw lies in tsupport w). A continuous map with compact support into a normed space is bounded (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), so there is L ∈ ℝ with ‖Dw(z)‖ ≤ L for every z ∈ ℝ^P. Put L₀ := max(L, 0). Then L₀ ≥ 0 and ‖Dw(z)‖ ≤ L₀ for every z.

4. (Mean value inequality.) ℝ^P is convex, w is differentiable at every point, and ‖Dw(z)‖ ≤ L₀ for every z. The mean value inequality (Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le with s = ℝ^P) therefore gives ‖w(x) − w(y)‖ ≤ L₀·‖x − y‖ for all x, y ∈ ℝ^P.

5. (Conclusion.) Put c := C·L₀, which is ≥ 0 as a product of nonnegative reals. For all x, y ∈ ℝ^P, step 1 (applied to β := w(x) − w(y)), step 4 and C ≥ 0 give
   |w(x) − w(y)| ≤ C·‖w(x) − w(y)‖ ≤ C·(L₀·‖x − y‖) = c·‖x − y‖ = c·dist(x, y).
This is the claim. ∎

  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ : ∃ L : ℝ, ∀ z, ‖fderiv ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) z‖ ≤ L :=
    Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support
      (f := fderiv ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) hcont hcs'

  have hmv : ∀ x y : Euclid P, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x -
      (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y‖ ≤ max L 0 * ‖x - y‖ := fun x y =>
    convex_univ.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_fderiv_le (fun z _ => hdiff z)
      (fun z _ => (hL z).trans (le_max_left _ _)) (mem_univ y) (mem_univ x)
  refine ⟨C * max L 0, mul_nonneg hC0 (le_max_right _ _), fun x y => ?_⟩
  have h1 := hC ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y)
  have h2 := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (hmv x y) hC0
  rw [dist_eq_norm]
  calc covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x -
        (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y)
      ≤ C * ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) y‖ := h1
    _ ≤ C * (max L 0 * ‖x - y‖) := h2
    _ = C * max L 0 * ‖x - y‖ := by ring
proof_key_steps: norm_props (iii): |β| ≤ C‖β‖ for every k-covector β, with C ≥ 0.
ω is C^∞ with compact support, so Dω is continuous with compact support; hence ‖Dω(z)‖ ≤ L₀ for all z, with L₀ ≥ 0.
Mean value inequality on the convex set ℝ^P: ‖ω(x) − ω(y)‖ ≤ L₀‖x − y‖.
c := C·L₀ ≥ 0 gives |ω(x) − ω(y)| ≤ c·dist(x, y).

subproblems.title: A constant (n+1)-covector is the exterior derivative of its affine contraction (n+1)⁻¹·ι_{y−x₀}α
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an (n+1)-covector on ℝ^P (α : Covector (Euclid P) (n+1), a continuous alternating (n+1)-linear form) and let x₀ ∈ ℝ^P. Let ψ be the n-form ψ(y) := ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ · α.curryLeft(y − x₀), i.e. ψ(y)(v₁, …, v_n) = (n + 1)⁻¹ · α(y − x₀, v₁, …, v_n). Then for every x ∈ ℝ^P the exterior derivative of ψ at x equals α: extDeriv ψ x = α. Here extDeriv ψ x = alternatizeUncurryFin(fderiv ℝ ψ x) is Mathlib's exterior derivative, which is SimonGMT's exteriorDerivative.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (x₀ x : Euclid P), extDeriv (fun y : Euclid P => ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft (y - x₀)) x = α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof, first half: the homotopy formula for a constant form. With ψ(x) = (n+1)⁻¹·α.curryLeft(x − x₀), dψ(x) = α for every x.

Notation. α.curryLeft : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n is Mathlib's ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft, with α.curryLeft(v)(v₁, …, v_n) = α(v, v₁, …, v_n) (curryLeft_apply_apply). For an n-form ω, extDeriv ω x := alternatizeUncurryFin(fderiv ℝ ω x) (definition of Mathlib's extDeriv). Put s := ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹, L := α.curryLeft and ψ(y) := s · L(y − x₀).

1. (Derivative of the contraction.) L is a continuous linear map, so it has derivative L at every point, in particular at x − x₀ (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt). The map y ↦ y − x₀ has the identity as derivative at x (hasFDerivAt_id, HasFDerivAt.sub_const). By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp), y ↦ L(y − x₀) has derivative L ∘ id = L at x (ContinuousLinearMap.comp_id).

2. (Constant factor.) Multiplying by the constant s, ψ has derivative s • L at x (HasFDerivAt.const_smul). Hence fderiv ℝ ψ x = s • L (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).

3. (Pull out the scalar.) By definition, extDeriv ψ x = alternatizeUncurryFin(fderiv ℝ ψ x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(s • L) = s • alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul).

4. (Round trip.) ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft states alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) = (n + 1) • α, a natural-number multiple. Indeed alternatizeUncurryFin(f)(v₀, …, v_n) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i f(v_i)(v₀, …, v̂_i, …, v_n). For f = α.curryLeft each summand equals (−1)^i α(v_i, v₀, …, v̂_i, …, v_n) = (−1)^i (−1)^i α(v₀, …, v_n) = α(v₀, …, v_n), because moving v_i to the front costs the sign (−1)^i; so the sum is (n+1)·α(v₀, …, v_n). By Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul, (n + 1) • α = ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℝ) • α = ((n : ℝ) + 1) • α (push_cast).

5. (Conclusion.) Therefore extDeriv ψ x = s • (((n : ℝ) + 1) • α) = (s · ((n : ℝ) + 1)) • α (smul_smul). Since (n : ℝ) + 1 > 0, ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ · ((n : ℝ) + 1) = 1 (inv_mul_cancel₀), so this is 1 • α = α (one_smul). ∎

Lean note (this exact proof compiled against the pinned snapshot in a scratch file; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only):
  intro P n α x₀ x
  have h1 : HasFDerivAt (fun y : Euclid P => α.curryLeft (y - x₀)) α.curryLeft x := by
    have h := (α.curryLeft.hasFDerivAt (x := x - x₀)).comp x ((hasFDerivAt_id x).sub_const x₀)
    rw [ContinuousLinearMap.comp_id] at h
    exact h
  have hd : HasFDerivAt (fun y : Euclid P => ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft (y - x₀))
      (((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft) x := h1.const_smul (((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹)
  rw [extDeriv, hd.fderiv, ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_smul,
    ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft, ← Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul ℝ,
    smul_smul]
  have hn : ((n : ℝ) + 1) ≠ 0 := by positivity
  push_cast
  rw [inv_mul_cancel₀ hn, one_smul]
proof_key_steps: y ↦ α.curryLeft(y − x₀) has derivative α.curryLeft at x (chain rule: a continuous linear map composed with y ↦ y − x₀).
fderiv ℝ ψ x = (n+1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft (HasFDerivAt.const_smul).
extDeriv ψ x = alternatizeUncurryFin((n+1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft) = (n+1)⁻¹ • alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) (alternatizeUncurryFin_smul).
alternatizeUncurryFin(α.curryLeft) = (n+1) • α (alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft with Nat.cast_smul_eq_nsmul), so extDeriv ψ x = α.

subproblems.title: A current takes the same value on test forms that agree on an open neighbourhood of its support
subproblems.statement: Assume (VO), the exact frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support, which appears verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let P, k ∈ ℕ, let U and G be subsets of ℝ^P, let X ∈ 𝒟_k(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U k) be a current and let φ₁, φ₂ ∈ 𝒟^k(U) (TestFormOn U k) be test forms. Suppose G is open, spt X ⊆ G (X.support, Simon 6.2.11), and φ₁(x) = φ₂(x) for every x ∈ G. Then X(φ₁) = X(φ₂).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k) (φ₁ φ₂ : TestFormOn U k), IsOpen G → X.support ⊆ G → EqOn (φ₁ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) (φ₂ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) G → X φ₁ = X φ₂
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent proof (localization by (VO)), stated for two arbitrary test forms that agree on an open set G ⊇ spt X. In parent step 6 one takes U = ℝ^P, φ₁ = φ, φ₂ = ζφ and G = B_{ϱ+ε/2}(x₀).

1. (The difference is a test form.) TestFormOn U k is a submodule of the k-forms, so φ := φ₁ − φ₂ ∈ TestFormOn U k. Its underlying form is x ↦ φ₁(x) − φ₂(x) (Submodule.coe_sub).

2. (Where φ vanishes.) For x ∈ G, φ(x) = φ₁(x) − φ₂(x) = 0 by hypothesis. Hence support φ = {x : φ(x) ≠ 0} ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ G.

3. (Topological support.) G is open, so ℝ^P ∖ G is closed (IsOpen.isClosed_compl). A closed set containing support φ contains its closure, so tsupport φ = closure(support φ) ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ G (closure_minimal).

4. (Disjointness.) spt X = X.support ⊆ G and tsupport φ ⊆ ℝ^P ∖ G, and G and ℝ^P ∖ G are disjoint. Hence tsupport φ and spt X are disjoint (Disjoint.mono applied to disjoint_compl_left).

5. (Apply (VO).) (VO) with (P, k, U, S := X, ω := φ) gives X(φ) = 0.

6. (Linearity.) X acts through the linear map X.toCurrent, so X(φ₁ − φ₂) = X(φ₁) − X(φ₂) (LinearMap.map_sub). By step 5, X(φ₁) − X(φ₂) = 0, i.e. X(φ₁) = X(φ₂). ∎

Lean note (this exact proof compiled against the pinned snapshot in a scratch file; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only):
  intro VO P k U G X φ₁ φ₂ hG hspt heq
  have hsub : tsupport ((φ₁ - φ₂ : TestFormOn U k) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) ⊆ Gᶜ := by
    apply closure_minimal _ hG.isClosed_compl
    intro x hx hxG
    apply hx
    change (φ₁ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x - (φ₂ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x = 0
    rw [heq hxG, sub_self]
  have hdisj : Disjoint (tsupport ((φ₁ - φ₂ : TestFormOn U k) : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k))
      X.support :=
    Disjoint.mono hsub hspt disjoint_compl_left
  have h := VO P k U X (φ₁ - φ₂) hdisj
  have h2 := X.toCurrent.map_sub φ₁ φ₂
  change X (φ₁ - φ₂) = X φ₁ - X φ₂ at h2
  linarith
proof_key_steps: φ₁ − φ₂ is a test form in U that vanishes on G.
Gᶜ is closed, so tsupport(φ₁ − φ₂) ⊆ Gᶜ, which is disjoint from spt X ⊆ G.
(VO) gives X(φ₁ − φ₂) = 0, and linearity gives X(φ₁) = X(φ₂).

subproblems.title: A cycle supported in an open ball annihilates every test form that is constant on that ball
subproblems.statement: Assume (VO), the exact frozen statement of dtc_vanish_off_support, which appears verbatim as the first hypothesis of the Lean statement: for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every U ⊆ ℝ^P, every current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) whose topological support is disjoint from spt S, S(ω) = 0. Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let X ∈ 𝒟_{n+1}(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ (n+1)) be a current, x₀ ∈ ℝ^P, r a real number with r > 0, α an (n+1)-covector (Covector (Euclid P) (n+1)) and φ ∈ 𝒟^{n+1}(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ (n+1)) a test form. Suppose ∂X = 0 (X.boundary = 0), spt X ⊆ B_r(x₀) (the open ball), and φ(x) = α for every x ∈ B_r(x₀). Then X(φ) = 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n), Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) S.support → S ω = 0) → ∀ (P n : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)) (x₀ : Euclid P) (r : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)), 0 < r → X.boundary = 0 → X.support ⊆ ball x₀ r → (∀ x ∈ ball x₀ r, (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1)) x = α) → X φ = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5 and 7 of the parent proof (cut-off, and 'constant forms are boundaries near spt X'). Here the cut-off is taken at inner radius r, and the parent's test form ζα is replaced by any test form φ that equals α on B_r(x₀). The (VO)-localization of parent step 6 is the sibling localize, and the identity dψ = α is the sibling affine_primitive.

Notation. B_r(x₀) is the open ball and B̄_r(x₀) the closed ball. For an n-form g, dg = extDeriv g. For η ∈ TestFormOn univ n, exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n η ∈ TestFormOn univ (n+1) is the test form whose underlying form is extDeriv η.

1. (Cut-off.) Let ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ be Mathlib's smooth bump function (ContDiffBump) centred at x₀ with inner radius rIn := r and outer radius rOut := r + 1; this is allowed because 0 < r < r + 1. Then ζ is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff) and has compact support (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport; ℝ^P is finite-dimensional). Moreover ζ(z) = 1 for every z ∈ B̄_r(x₀) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall), hence for every z ∈ B_r(x₀) (ball_subset_closedBall).

2. (The primitive.) Let ψ(y) := ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ · α.curryLeft(y − x₀), an n-form. ψ is C^∞: it is the continuous linear map α.curryLeft composed with the smooth map y ↦ y − x₀, multiplied by a constant (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff, ContDiff.comp, contDiff_id.sub contDiff_const, ContDiff.const_smul). By the sibling affine_primitive, extDeriv ψ y = α for every y ∈ ℝ^P.

3. (A compactly supported primitive.) Let g(y) := ζ(y) · ψ(y). g is C^∞ (ContDiff.smul applied to steps 1 and 2), and it has compact support because ζ does (HasCompactSupport.smul_right). So g is a test form with tsupport g ⊆ ℝ^P = univ, and hence η := g ∈ TestFormOn univ n.

4. (∂X = 0 kills dη.) Let dη := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n η; its underlying form is extDeriv g. By the definition of the boundary (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), X(dη) = (∂X)(η). Since ∂X = 0, X(dη) = 0(η) = 0.

5. (φ = dη on the ball.) Let y ∈ B_r(x₀). The open ball B_r(x₀) is a neighbourhood of y (isOpen_ball.mem_nhds). For z in it ζ(z) = 1 (step 1), so g(z) = ψ(z); thus g =ᶠ[𝓝 y] ψ. The exterior derivative at y depends only on the germ at y (Filter.EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq), so extDeriv g y = extDeriv ψ y = α by step 2. By hypothesis φ(y) = α. Hence φ(y) = (dη)(y) for every y ∈ B_r(x₀).

6. (Localization.) B_r(x₀) is open, spt X ⊆ B_r(x₀) by hypothesis, and by step 5 the forms φ, dη ∈ TestFormOn univ (n+1) agree on B_r(x₀). The sibling localize, applied with (VO), P, k := n + 1, U := univ, G := B_r(x₀), X, φ₁ := φ and φ₂ := dη, gives X(φ) = X(dη). By step 4, X(dη) = 0. Hence X(φ) = 0. ∎

Lean note (this exact proof compiled against the pinned snapshot in a scratch file, using only the two siblings; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound only):
  intro VO P n X x₀ r α φ hr hbd hspt hφ
  let ζ : ContDiffBump x₀ := ⟨r, r + 1, hr, by linarith⟩
  let ψ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n := fun y => ((n : ℝ) + 1)⁻¹ • α.curryLeft (y - x₀)
  have hψ : IsSmoothForm ψ :=
    (α.curryLeft.contDiff.comp (contDiff_id.sub contDiff_const)).const_smul _
  let g : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n := fun y => ζ y • ψ y
  have hg : IsSmoothForm g := ζ.contDiff.smul hψ
  have hgc : HasCompactSupport g := ζ.hasCompactSupport.smul_right
  let η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n := ⟨g, ⟨hg, hgc⟩, subset_univ _⟩
  have h0 : X (exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n η) = 0 := by
    have h := congrArg (fun T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n => T η) hbd
    simpa using h
  have heq : EqOn (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1))
      ((exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ n η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (n + 1)) :
        DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (n + 1)) (ball x₀ r) := by
    intro y hy
    rw [hφ y hy]
    change α = extDeriv g y
    have hev : g =ᶠ[𝓝 y] ψ := by
      filter_upwards [isOpen_ball.mem_nhds hy] with z hz
      simp [g, ζ.one_of_mem_closedBall (ball_subset_closedBall hz)]
    rw [hev.extDeriv_eq, Submission.cbrld_cone_extDeriv_affine_contraction P n α x₀ y]
  rw [Submission.cbrld_cone_eval_eq_of_eqOn_open VO P (n + 1) univ (ball x₀ r) X φ _ isOpen_ball hspt heq, h0]
proof_key_steps: Bump ζ (ContDiffBump at x₀, rIn = r, rOut = r + 1): smooth, compactly supported, ζ = 1 on B_r(x₀).
ψ(y) = (n+1)⁻¹ α.curryLeft(y − x₀) is smooth with dψ = α (affine_primitive); η := ζψ is a test n-form.
∂X = 0 gives X(dη) = ∂X(η) = 0.
On the open ball ζψ = ψ, so dη = dψ = α = φ there (EventuallyEq.extDeriv_eq).
localize with G = B_r(x₀) ⊇ spt X gives X(φ) = X(dη) = 0.
